t: This is St Anne's Limehouse, an Anglican church in Tower Hamlets. It was consecrated in 1730, and is one of the twelve churches built under the 1711 Act of Parliament. Its architect was Nicholas Hawksmoor, a leading figure of English Baroque in the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. He worked alongside Christopher Wren and John Vanbrugh, and contributed to St Paul's Cathedral, Greenwich Hospital, Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard. Here in Limehouse, you can see his hand at work in a church of his own.
